why: This keeps TLC runs small and counterexamples attributable while retaining interaction coverage for the highest-risk journal and concurrency promises.

why: The implementation cannot refine a fair pending-resolution contract if its own Spec permits permanent stuttering while blocked.

decision: Retained four additive red witnesses for scope concurrency, retry object identity, unavailable receipts, and stale recovery cleanup.
why: Each model finding has a cheap deterministic execution path in current TypeScript or hook behavior.

decision: Required one NoGuard configuration per behavior and exact TLC exit code 12 plus invariant-name matching.
why: A passing hardened model is meaningful only when each protection can independently affect its named promise.

why: This separates absence of the required guard from claims about exploitability that the trial did not establish.
